title: Multimodal Hivemind: Do Vision-Language Models Share the Same Caption Blind Spots?

original_idea.body:
# Multimodal Hivemind: Do Vision-Language Models Share the Same Caption Blind Spots?

**Problem:** Success state: deployers of VLMs in safety-relevant settings know whether different VLMs share the same perceptual blind spots.

**Direction:** On a fixed image set including safety-relevant cases, get captions/safety-classifications from several open VLMs. Identify images where ALL models share the same error or omission.

**Why it matters:** If every VLM misreads the same images, automated visual moderation has correlated holes an adversary can exploit across platforms at once.

**Relevant context:** Direct multimodal follow-up flagged in Artificial Hivemind 'multimodal'. Open VLMs (LLaVA, Qwen-VL).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlated VLM perceptual blind spots create cross-platform moderation holes, a concrete exploitable scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run several open VLMs on public images, measure agreement; guided, mentor helpful for labeling errors.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (universal blind-spot images); some labeling effort across models.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Under-studied multimodal surface, public VLMs, independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: VLM inference on a single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Correlated VLM perceptual blind spots across models appear largely unmeasured.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Correlated VLM perceptual blind spots across models appear largely unmeasured.
